open_points.subject: ConnectionRecord
open_points.text: a connection record the owner has confirmed
open_points.question: What facts constitute a connection record, is it a value or entity, who mints it, and from what identity inputs?
options: An entity minted by the deliverer from project id plus normalized folder bindings
A value supplied by the agent and merely validated by the deliverer
An entity identified only by project id
open_points.default_guess: An entity minted by the deliverer and identified by project id, containing the confirmed root and photo-folder binding.

open_points.subject: ConnectionRecord confirmation
open_points.text: a connection record the owner has confirmed; delivery becomes possible for that project
open_points.question: Is confirmation a status of an existing connection, part of its immutable creation facts, or a separate owner-produced record, and which action changes it?
options: The connect action creates an already-confirmed connection
A connection is created unconfirmed and a separate action confirms it
Confirmation is a separate immutable owner-attestation value
open_points.default_guess: The connect action atomically creates an already-confirmed connection.

open_points.subject: Folder binding
open_points.text: a connection whose subfolder is written to leave its root is refused, a photo folder linked outside the root is refused when it is used
open_points.question: Which root, subfolder and resolved photo-folder facts belong to the connection model, and is the linked-folder target captured at connection time or read again when used?
options: Store root and relative subfolder; resolve the current linked target when used
Store the resolved photo-folder target when connecting
Store both the written binding and the confirmed resolved target
open_points.default_guess: Store both the written root/subfolder binding and the resolved target confirmed at connection time.

witness.initial: A confirmed connection's photo subfolder is a link to a folder inside the root.
events: The owner connects the object through the agent.
Syncthing or the owner replaces the link so that it points outside the root.
The calling flow scans the project.
outcomes: The scan rereads the link target and refuses the connection.
The scan uses the target captured in the connection record and continues.
witness.observer: The owner through the calling flow

open_points.subject: SourceFile
open_points.text: each file with a status: ready, placed or published with its source id, or rejected with a reason
open_points.question: What makes two observations the same source file when a name, metadata or bytes can be replaced?
options: Folder connection plus file name
Project plus source-content identity
Project plus file name plus observed metadata
A deliverer-minted observation id
open_points.default_guess: Treat the listed file as a value observation, while source content is identified within a project by a digest of the observed bytes.

witness.initial: A scan reports ready.jpg as ready.
events: Syncthing replaces ready.jpg with different bytes and metadata.
outcomes: The second result is the same source file with changed facts.
The second result is a different source file despite sharing the name.

open_points.subject: SourceId
open_points.text: project id, file name, source id, Portal photo id
open_points.question: Who mints the source id, from what facts, and does the calling flow merely return an id previously issued by a scan or choose one itself?
options: The deliverer derives and returns it from project and source content
The calling flow supplies an opaque id that the deliverer binds to content
Syncthing or another upstream source supplies it
It is identical to the file name
open_points.default_guess: The deliverer derives a stable source id from project id and source content during scanning, and the calling flow echoes it on later operations.

open_points.subject: FileMetadata
open_points.text: file names, file metadata and bytes
open_points.question: Which metadata facts cross the boundary and become model facts, and which model owns them?
options: Only modification time
Filesystem metadata including modification time, size and type
Filesystem metadata plus parsed camera metadata
An opaque metadata record whose facts are defined later
open_points.default_guess: Model the metadata actually used by State 0: modification time plus the camera-record date when present; do not make unrelated filesystem metadata domain facts.

open_points.subject: PhotoDate
open_points.text: The photo date comes from the camera record, otherwise from the file's modification time
open_points.question: What model fact is the camera record, who produces it, and is the selected photo date retained as a value with its provenance or only as a bare date?
options: A bare selected date derived by the deliverer
A date value carrying camera-record or modification-time provenance
An untrusted source-metadata entity retained separately
open_points.default_guess: Use a value containing the selected date and whether it came from the camera record or modification time.

open_points.subject: DeliveryStatus
open_points.text: each file with a status: ready, placed or published with its source id, or rejected with a reason
open_points.question: Does every status carry a source id, or only ready, placed and published while rejected carries only a reason?
options: Every status carries a source id; rejected additionally carries a reason
Only ready, placed and published carry a source id; rejected carries a reason
Source id and reason are independently optional fields
open_points.default_guess: Every observed file carries its source id, and rejected additionally carries a reason.

witness.initial: A visible file has readable metadata but unsupported or invalid bytes.
events: The calling flow scans the project.
outcomes: The rejected item contains both its source id and rejection reason.
The rejected item contains only its rejection reason.

open_points.subject: DeliveryStatus
open_points.text: a status: ready, placed or published with its source id, or rejected with a reason
open_points.question: Are these persistent lifecycle states of one entity or results computed independently by each scan, and can a rejected item later become ready after the file changes?
options: Persistent states with defined transitions
Computed scan classifications with no stored lifecycle
Placed and published are persistent, while ready and rejected are computed
open_points.default_guess: Placed and published are persistent facts; ready and rejected are computed classifications of the current file observation.

witness.initial: A file is rejected during a scan.
events: Syncthing replaces its bytes with a deliverable image under the same name.
outcomes: The same item remains in the terminal rejected state.
The current observation is reported ready.

open_points.subject: Placement
open_points.text: One placement exists per project and source content; repeating it changes nothing.
open_points.question: Is a placement an entity or value, who mints it, and is its identity project plus source content, project plus source id, or the returned file reference?
options: An entity keyed by project and source-content identity
An entity keyed by project and source id
A value identified by its file reference
open_points.default_guess: A deliverer-minted entity identified by project id plus source-content identity, with source id and file reference as facts.

open_points.subject: Placement content binding
open_points.text: a file whose content differs from the chosen one is not placed
open_points.question: What immutable observation identifies the chosen content between scan and delivery, and is that observation represented by source id, metadata, a content identity, or another model?
options: Source id commits to the exact content
A separate content identity from the scan commits to the bytes
File metadata commits to the observed version
Delivery rereads by name without an earlier content commitment
open_points.default_guess: The scan-issued source id commits to an exact source-content digest that delivery must revalidate.

witness.initial: A scan reports photo.jpg as ready.
events: The calling flow chooses that result.
Syncthing replaces photo.jpg with different bytes before delivery.
The calling flow requests delivery using the reported file name and source id.
outcomes: The source id binds the old bytes, so delivery refuses the replacement.
The source id is only an external label, so the replacement is prepared and placed.
witness.observer: The owner through the calling flow

open_points.subject: PreparedImage
open_points.text: a prepared image in the Portal store, its reference and the publication body
open_points.question: Is the prepared image a value of the placement or a separately identified entity, and what facts connect it to the source content, file reference and publication body?
options: A value embedded in the placement result
A separate entity identified by the store reference
The placement entity itself, with prepared-image facts
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as the immutable output value of a placement entity, addressed by the returned store reference.

open_points.subject: FileReference
open_points.text: statuses, file reference, publication body
open_points.question: Who mints the file reference, what model does it identify, and is it stable across repeated delivery?
options: The deliverer mints a stable reference identifying the placement's prepared image
The Portal binary store mints it
It is a reproducible value derived from project and source content
A new reference may be returned on each delivery
open_points.default_guess: The deliverer mints and persists one stable reference for the prepared image when the placement is first created.

open_points.subject: PublicationBody
open_points.text: a prepared image in the Portal store, its reference and the publication body
open_points.question: Is the publication body an immutable value generated from the placement, what facts does it represent, and is the exact first body returned on repeated delivery?
options: An immutable value stored with the placement
A value regenerated from current source metadata on every read
A caller-owned value merely passed through by the deliverer
open_points.default_guess: An immutable deliverer-generated value stored with and returned from the placement.

open_points.subject: Repeated delivery result
open_points.text: the first result, nothing written
open_points.question: Which model is retained as the first result, and does repeating delivery read that persisted result or reconstruct an equivalent result from current facts?
options: Persist and return the original DeliveryResult value
Reconstruct an equivalent result from the existing placement
Return only the existing placement identity
open_points.default_guess: Persist the original delivery result and return that same logical value without observing changed source metadata.

witness.initial: A photo has been delivered successfully.
events: Its source metadata changes without changing its bytes.
The calling flow delivers the same source again.
outcomes: The original publication body and other result facts are returned.
A reconstructed result reflects the changed metadata.

open_points.subject: Failed delivery mutation
open_points.text: a photo that cannot be delivered is reported with its reason and no placement is made
open_points.question: May a failed delivery create or change any durable model other than a placement, such as a rejection record or status, or must all model state remain unchanged?
options: No durable model changes
A rejection result or status may be persisted
Attempt and diagnostic records may be created but delivery-domain state cannot change
open_points.default_guess: No delivery-domain model changes; the rejection is a returned value only.

witness.initial: A ready file has no placement.
outcomes: A later scan reports a persisted rejected status.
A later scan recomputes status without any remembered failure.

open_points.subject: Publication
open_points.text: the file is reported as published, with its Portal photo id
open_points.question: What model records publication, is it an entity or a state of the placement, who mints it, and which identity binds the Portal photo id to the source?
options: A separate publication entity minted by the deliverer
A published state and Portal photo id added to the placement
An immutable value record keyed by source id
open_points.default_guess: Publication is a state transition of the placement, recorded by the deliverer with the Portal-minted photo id.

open_points.subject: Published status timing
open_points.text: Publish a placed photo (Portal operation, by the calling flow)
open_points.question: Does a photo become published in the deliverer's model when the Portal creates its record or only when the calling flow successfully performs Record the publication?
options: At Portal publication time
Only when Record the publication succeeds
Portal publication and recording form one logical state change
open_points.default_guess: Only the Record the publication action changes the deliverer's placement to published.

witness.initial: A placement exists and is reported placed.
events: The calling flow publishes it successfully in the Portal.
The calling flow has not yet recorded the resulting Portal photo id.
The calling flow scans the project.
outcomes: The file is reported published because the Portal operation occurred.
The file remains placed because publication has not been recorded.

open_points.subject: PortalPhotoId binding
open_points.text: a different photo id for the same source is refused and nothing is changed
open_points.question: Does “same source” mean the source id, the project-and-source-content placement identity, the file name, or another model identity?
options: The same source id globally
The same project and source-content placement
The same file name within a connection
The same prepared-image reference
open_points.default_guess: It means the same placement identity: project id plus source-content identity.

open_points.subject: ProjectId and PortalPhotoId
open_points.text: project id, file name, source id, Portal photo id
open_points.question: Which identifiers are foreign values versus entities owned by the deliverer, and who mints each one from what?
options: ProjectId and PortalPhotoId are opaque foreign values; SourceId is deliverer-minted
All are opaque caller-supplied values
The deliverer owns project and source identities but Portal owns PortalPhotoId
open_points.default_guess: Treat ProjectId as an opaque upstream value, PortalPhotoId as a Portal-minted opaque value, file name as untrusted input, and SourceId as deliverer-minted.
